r3_note: D10 was paired across readers by time but the two rows are different slips: r1's D10 is the missing verb at 59:09 (ذكّرني خبز, Amal 'To bring.'), r2's D10 row is the same slip as r1's D11 (تجيبي -> أجيب). Both are kept as separate rows: D10 = missing verb (PROPOSE), D11 = person on the verb (B18). D8 (بنغير -> نغير) is a second, separate slip inside the A15 moment: A15 fixed the tense (past غيّرنا), D8 is the b- he then left on after لازم. D6 and D12 are dropped as the same moment as A12 / A27 (GR-28). Audio check suggested for 30:20 (D7): Amal said 'your mind.' after his شو غيّر رأيك - he may have said ra2yi (my), but the engine wrote the right form twice.

rows.medi_said: بدأت شغلي على تـ- تسعة ونص.
rows.why: Clock time needs el-saa3a / el- before the number; Amal only redirected the question (من وين) and let the time form pass.
rows.english: I started my work at nine thirty.

rows.medi_said: معروف is ground؟ معروف؟ No. ... خروف is lamb. مرفوف؟ What was What was ground؟
rows.why: He attempted معروف (known) and the non-word مرفوف for 'ground (meat)' and asked 'What was ground?' - he tried wrong words before asking, so tier 1 not a pure didn't-know (tier 0); Amal supplied مفروم. Sheet: 'ground beef | La7meh mafrumeh | لحمة مفرومة'.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same moment; he produced wrong words (معروف, مرفوف) before asking, so it is a wrong-word slip (tier 1) with signal asked, not a never-attempted didn't-know. t set to the line where he gives up and asks (04:05), which Amal answers at 04:11.

rows.why: Collective/feminine خضرا takes a feminine adjective; he wavered and settled on masculine مختلف, Amal let it pass (my reading).

rows.amal_said: Yeah, we don't say that yesterday. Just yesterday is its own...
rows.why: امبارح never takes el-; Amal had modeled نفس مبارح at 05:27 and then explained the rule; his 05:37 نفس امبارح repeated her model.
rows.r3_challenge: Looks like a self-fix before her help (GR-22): at 05:32 he said نفس الامبارح and at 05:37 said نفس امبارح himself; Amal's 'Yeah, we don't say that yesterday' came after, at 05:41, confirming his fixed form. (Her 05:27 line 'نفس من بارح' came before his slip, not as a fix of it.)

rows.why: Telling what happened yesterday he used the present form أجي; Amal recast past أجا and he repeated it.
Came TO my house takes على/عند, not من (from); Amal said أجا على and then سأجا عندي يعني; he repeated أجا على بيتي.

rows.medi_said: Uh, but fatad means, like, you choose? ... So I know bafadal. Is it one of my words?
rows.why: Amal asked 'امتى بتفضل؟' (08:46); he did not recognise it (thought it meant 'you choose') and asked; she explained 'when do you prefer' and 'بفضل I prefer' - a sheet word ('i prefer | Ana bafaddel | أنا بفضل') he did not catch on listening.
rows.r3_why: Real listening miss with an explicit question from him and Amal's voiced explanation; he then used it right (09:30 أنا بفضل أعمل). Tier 0 since he produced no wrong Arabic word of his own.

rows.why: Amal asked 'حبيت إنت امبارح كيف اتدربنا' (10:36); he answered with her verb heard as حكيتلي (you told me) - a mishearing of her word - and she repeated حبيت, then re-asked the whole question (10:58) and he answered in English 'Oh yeah, yeah. نفس الطريقة'.
rows.english: did you like (how we practised yesterday)
rows.r3_why: He echoed her question word wrongly, which is a listening miss (he misheard حبيت), so mode = listening as r2 had; the transcript shows no intent of his own to say 'you told me'.

rows.why: Defining بكسر as a habit ('I make something broken') needs the ordinary present with b- (أنا بخلّي); he used bare خلّي and Amal let it pass with 'طيب' (right form is my reading).
rows.r3_why: The line is clear in the transcript (11:26-11:35, split over turns) and nothing between أنا and خلّي drops the b-; Amal gave no fix, so grammar-B for her review.

rows.medi_said: بتكسر. ما بتكسري. ما، ما بتس-- بتكس،
rows.chat: e7na benfaddel enno inti ma tekserih
rows.why: After بنفضل انه (we prefer that) the verb drops b-; Amal recast ما تكسري and he said ما تكسريه.
rows.english: We prefer that you don't break it

rows.why: 'I broke it' needs the object ending -o on the verb; Amal recast كسرته and he repeated it.
For 'what broke them' (doer + object) he used the n- (get-broken) form انكسروهم/انكسرهم; Amal recast the plain transitive كسرهم.

rows.amal_said: تكسري. What's plural of أشي إشي؟ ... تكسري أشياء.
rows.why: 'things' is plural; Amal asked for the plural of إشي and gave أشياء; he then said تكسري شي, not taking it.
rows.english: Since when do you break things?

rows.why: سنين = years, not teeth; Amal said سنان and asked what سنين is, he answered 'year' and said سنانها.

He had just settled the plural كاسات at 20:27, then produced كسرات (a plural of cup blended with كسر); Amal recast 'Kasat' and he said 'كاسات، that's right'. Wrong form of a word he knows (sheet: 'cup | Kaasa | كاسة') = tier 2.
rows.r3_why: Same slip for both readers; he was aiming at the plural of كاسة, which he had just said right, and built a wrong plural shape - tier 2 (wrong form of a known word) fits better than tier 1 (different lexical item).

rows.why: قاتل takes بعض directly (each other), not مع بعض (together); Amal had said قتلوا بعض, he added مع, she restated 'fought each other' and he dropped مع.
'One of the kids' needs من; Amal prompted 'واحد of the children' and he said واحد من ولاد.
'I change MY mind' needs the possessive ending رأيي; Amal recast and he repeated (sheet: i change my mind | Ba8ayyer ra2yi).

rows.medi_said: We should... Okay. احنا كان لازم--
rows.amal_said: we just should. we not should have. we
rows.why: كان لازم means 'should have'; for plain 'we should' Amal said 'we just should, not should have' and he said احنا لازم.
rows.english: We should change the flight time

rows.why: After لازم the verb is a bare present, not past غيّرنا; Amal named the rule 'present. مضارع' (laazem_noun clue).

In 'احنا لازم ...' the verb after لازم drops its b-; after Amal told him to use the present (31:42, A15 = the past-tense slip) he said بنغير, she recast نغير and he repeated نغير (31:53). A separate slip from A15: that one was the tense, this one is the b-.
rows.r3_why: Real voiced recast with his immediate repeat; it is a new error (b- kept after لازم) produced after A15's tense fix, not a repeat of the same phrase, so it is its own B2 row.

rows.medi_said: The time of the flight. وقت ال... اه... flight. Oh my God.
rows.why: He could not find طيارة; Amal hinted 'remember car?' (سيارة) and he said طيارة - a didn't-know prompt.

rows.amal_said: very close. بس السيارة، السيارة feminine or masculine؟ غيرت.
rows.why: Feminine subject طيارة needs feminine past تغيرت; Amal asked feminine or masculine and he said تغيرت.

rows.amal_said: Program is masculine. ... Program is not feminine.
rows.why: برنامج is masculine so the verb is تغير; Amal said 'Program is masculine' and he said تغير.
After لازم a bare present verb is needed, not past اتغيروا; Amal recast يتغيروا, he asked 'is that past tense?' and took it.

rows.amal_said: تغير أو تغيري حالك أو حالك. Make it consistent. Make the gender consistent.
rows.why: The negative command to her must be feminine تغيري to match حالِك; Amal named the gender-consistency rule and he said ما تغيري حالك.
The first word of an idafa takes no el-: يوم الاجتماع; he started اليوم, Amal prompted 'day of the meeting' and he said يوم الاجتماع.
rows.english: why did the meeting day change?

rows.amal_said: did change. Why did it change? It did change.
rows.why: 'Why did it change' is past; he said present بتغيّر, Amal stressed 'It did change' and he said تغير.
rows.english: Why did the meeting day change?

rows.why: The command 'photograph me' is صوريني, not the present/t-form تصوريني; Amal said 'Again... You photograph me' and he said صوريني.

rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. That's the error I was talking about. So cam takes singular.
rows.why: After كم the noun is singular; Amal named the rule and he said كم صورة.
rows.english: How many pictures did you take?

rows.why: 'Do you get photographed a lot' needs the t- (get-X) form بتتصوري; Amal recast it and he said 'Oh, that's right, بتتصوري'.
rows.english: Do you get photographed a lot?

rows.why: 'Is there someone who knows' takes the ordinary present with b- (بيعرف, as in her chat and her own 54:15 'بيعرف يصور'); the engine wrote يعرف and Amal gave no fix - low because the engine often loses a short bi- (right form is my reading).
rows.english: is there someone who knows (how to photograph here)
rows.r3_why: Possible let-pass B1 slip; Amal's voiced lines model بيعرف but never point at his يعرف, so it can only be a grammar-B row, low confidence for the engine risk.

rows.amal_said: First do the left, left past. Make it past.
rows.why: Telling a past trip he used the bare لف; Amal said 'Make it past' and he said لما لفيت.
rows.english: When I traveled around the world

rows.proposed_rule: After remind / ask / tell someone, say the action as a verb before the thing: zakkreeni ajib 5ubez (remind me to bring bread), not zakkreeni 5ubez.
rows.why: For 'Remind me to bring bread' he went from the command straight to the thing (ذكّرني خبز); Amal supplied the missing verb in English ('To bring.', PG-22) and he added a verb (59:14 ذكريني تجيبي). Same shape as GR-27 (laazem needs a verb), but no bucket covers 'remind me + verb', so PROPOSE.
rows.r3_why: r1's D10 row (missing verb at 59:09) is real: his sentence lacked the verb and Amal's English 'To bring.' was a voiced prompt that he acted on. r2's D10 row (تجيبي -> أجيب, B18) is a different slip in the same exchange and is the same as r1's D11 - ruled there.

rows.amal_said: I bring. ... To bring, but who's bringing? You are bringing.
rows.why: In 'remind me to bring' the one bringing is him, so the verb is the I-form أجيب, not the you-form تجيبي; Amal said 'I bring' (59:19) and asked 'who's bringing? You are bringing' (59:27), and he fixed it to أجيب (59:33).
rows.r3_why: Both readers have this slip (r2 filed it under D10); clear voiced prompt and his fix to أجيب. t_amal = her first signal 'I bring.' at 59:19.

rows.why: For 'I reminded him' he put the you-ending -ak; Amal repeated 'I reminded him' and he moved to Zakaretno, then her Zakarto.
'They didn't remember me' needs ما; Amal said 'Didn't' and he said ما تذكّروني.
A habit ('he doesn't remember names') is present with b-; he used the past, Amal recast Ma bietzakar and he said 'Oh, it's present tense'.
Amal replaced his plural أسامي with أسماء (her chat el-asmaa2) - plural pattern; أسامي is also heard in Levantine, so medium.
rows.r3_challenge: أسامي is a normal Levantine plural of اسم; Amal's 'Asma' (1:02:44) runs straight into her real point, the missing el- ('As it's general, so what do we add?'), which is already A31. Her 'Asma' may be her own form rather than a vocab fix - check whether she counts أسامي as wrong.

rows.why: Names in general take el-; Amal asked what we add, he said 'I don't know', she gave Il asma.
